**Observations:**

- Layer 1 background pixels (row 0 except cols 12–15, the first/last 2–4 columns of most rows, the extreme corners, rows 26–27 at cols 0–3 and 24–27) sit at tiny values in ±0.036, i.e. essentially the untouched PyTorch‑style uniform initialization (±1/√784 ≈ 0.0357). This is exactly what is expected for pixels that are always zero in the data and never receive gradient (no weight decay).
- The trained region forms a contiguous, spatially smooth blob: rows 1–3 at cols ~3–23, rows 4–25 almost full width, rows 26–27 at cols ~4–23. The bottom row is more heavily trained than the top row; the right edge (col 27) is somewhat more trained than col 0. This footprint (objects filling the frame, content on rows 1–2 and row 27) is consistent with a Fashion‑MNIST‑like dataset rather than MNIST digits.
- Largest |W1| values ≈ 0.5–0.6 and all occur in coherent vertical strips shared across several units: right edge cols 23–26 at rows 4–11 (unit 12 up to +0.596, units 0/1/6/8/10 ≈ −0.4 to −0.5, units 11/15 ≈ +0.4–0.5), a second right-edge strip at rows 16–23 (units 4, 8, 7, 13, 14 positive; unit 11 ≈ −0.47), a left strip at col 4 rows 6–11 for unit 10 (+0.43) mirrored negatively on the right, a left blob rows 12–14 cols 5–6 for unit 12 (+0.41–0.44), a bottom band rows 25–26 (units 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 negative, unit 7 positive ≈ +0.4). Every large weight varies smoothly with its neighbours in both directions; I found no isolated single‑pixel or small‑patch spike, no pixel whose weight is large while its neighbours are at init, and no corner/edge patch with unexpected magnitude.
- Mild sign correlation: pixels in rows 1–2 (top shoulder region) have positive weights in ~13–14 of 16 units, but this is explainable (those pixels indicate "a top garment" shared by many classes) and is not accompanied by any anomalous magnitude.
- b1 is moderate (−0.38 … +0.41), no unit is dead or saturated; every hidden unit has a structured, non‑trivial W1 column. W2 entries are all within ±0.98 with mixed signs per unit, no row/column dominates, b2 is small (±0.35). No duplicated rows, no exact zeros/constants, no out‑of‑scale values.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 25%
